headline: A Faster Model, Floods Recede, and Ice at a Low
summary:
This week began with a developer story. Claude Haiku 5.5 became generally available on the Claude API, with improved tool use and lower latency. Alongside it, the Files API gained PDF page ranges, and Anthropic announced a new office in Seoul. Together they point to steady, practical progress for people who build small tools on the API.

The wider world had a mixed week. Flood waters began to recede in northern Italy, the United Nations warned that road closures were delaying aid convoys, and satellite data showed the smallest September Arctic sea ice on record. Three major central banks left interest rates unchanged.

Closer to home, Atlanta saw a Midtown office building approved for conversion to homes and a neighborhood group open a community garden. In architecture, a timber library that doubles as a flood barrier drew attention, and Houston's starting center was listed as questionable heading into the season.
